title: Can a chessboard colouring show a grid cannot be tiled?
description: A grid of five rows and three columns has the middle square of its top row removed, and it is coloured like a chessboard with white corners. Eight white and six black squares are left, but every tile covers one of each, so no tiling exists. Keeko's doubt, that an even count is enough, is struck.
teaching_notes: One idea: every tile covers one white and one black square, so the two colour counts must be equal. Watch for students who think an even number of squares is enough.

source: A 5 × 3 grid has the middle square of its top row removed. C
video_script.why: The child sees that colouring the squares gives a reason why a grid cannot be tiled.
video_script.substitution: Each tile covers one white and one black square, so n tiles cover n white and n black squares.
video_script.anchor: A grid of unit squares with 5 rows and 3 columns, its top middle square removed, coloured like a chessboard with white corners, and a tile that covers 2 squares.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks fourteen is even, so this grid can be tiled. But an even count is needed and may not be enough, because the two colour counts must also be equal.
video_script.payoff_line: No, the grid cannot be tiled, because eight white and six black squares are left.

final_answer.value: Not tileable: 8 white and 6 black squares remain, but every tile covers one of each
final_answer.spoken: no, because eight white and six black squares remain, but every tile covers one of each

hold_back: Not tileable: 8 white and 6 black squares remain, but every tile covers one of each
maths_rules: With white corners, the full 5 × 3 grid has 8 white and 7 black squares.
The top middle square sits between two white corners, so it is black.
After removing it, 8 white and 6 black squares are left.
Each tile covers two neighbouring squares, and neighbours have different colours, so each tile covers one white and one black.
7 tiles would cover 7 white and 7 black squares, but there are 8 white and 6 black.
Slip: an even count of squares is needed, but it is not enough.
video_script.design: One grid coloured like a chessboard. The colours are counted before and after the square is removed, and compared with what the tiles would cover. The slip is thinking an even count is enough.
